extracted.intended_audience: news organizations (radio, television, digital), networks, syndication/program services, and students planning to enter the Edward R. Murrow Awards
extracted.subtask_short: Edward R. Murrow Awards entry rules
extracted.subtask_description: Official entry and judging rules for submitting work to the Edward R. Murrow Awards, covering eligibility, submission requirements, divisions/regions, fees, payment, judging standards, deadlines, and the dissent/review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — who may enter
rubrics_metrics.description: News stations, networks, syndication services, program services, and digital news organizations are all eligible to enter the awards. Edward R. Murrow Awards are presented to news organizations, not individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student Awards and other divisions exist (see Divisions). Entrants should confirm which division/category fits their organization type; awards themselves are given to organizations rather than named to individual reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry appearance requirement (timeframe and first-published rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must be submitted as first heard on air or viewed online. All entries must have appeared between January 1 and December 31 of the prior calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure the work's first airing/public posting date falls within the specified calendar-year window; entries that do not meet the timeframe are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisions & categories — correct division/region submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must be submitted in the proper division and region to be considered for judging. Entrants that do not enter correctly will be disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include Local TV and Radio; Network, Syndication Service, Program Service TV and Radio; Digital News Organizations; and Student Awards. Consult the Full Division & Category Information to select the appropriate category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market size determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Market size is determined by MSA ranking for radio entries and by DMA ranking for television entries, at the time the contest opens. RTDNA listings for DMA rankings are final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RTDNA reserves the sole right to reclassify the submission without prior notice to the entrant — confirm market classification at contest open to avoid unexpected reclassification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and late-entry policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Early Bird Deadline (with discounted pricing) and the Final Entry Deadline are fixed; late entries (additional fee applies: $55 per entry) will be accepted through a final late-entry cutoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 2026 the Early Bird Deadline is Jan. 20 (5 p.m. Eastern), the Final Entry Deadline is Feb. 19 (5 p.m. Eastern), and late entries accepted through Feb. 23 (5 p.m. Eastern) with $55 late fee per entry. Submit before the relevant deadline to avoid late fees and to receive discounted pricing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry fees and member discount eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry fees vary by division, market size, and membership status (member vs. non-member). To qualify for member rates on entry fees, a member of your full-time news staff must be an RTDNA member through the end of the entry period. Memberships must be paid in full at the time of entry. Entries in the cart do not qualify for discounted pricing if payment is received after the date of a rate change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to published fee tables for Early Bird and Regular Entry Fees by category (Radio small/large, Radio network, TV small/large, TV network, Digital). Verify staff membership status and payment timing before checkout to ensure member rates apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment methods and refund policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All entries are non-refundable. Payment must be made online by Visa, MasterCard or American Express at the time of entry. For totals in excess of $1,500, payment may be made by check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks must include the entry confirmation number(s). RTDNA must receive your check within two weeks of the close of the entry period for your entries to be considered. Make checks payable to the Radio Television Digital News Association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging standards — basis and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: The RTDNA Code of Ethics serves as the basis for judging standards. The decisions of the judges are final. At the discretion of the judges, awards may not be granted in some categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should review the RTDNA Code of Ethics as the principal evaluative framework. Judges have discretion both to select winners and to withhold awards in categories where standards are not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissent / Review Process for awarded works
rubrics_metrics.description: If individuals have concerns related to the process or other components of an Edward R. Murrow Award-winning work, RTDNA has established a Review Process. All concerns must be submitted through the RTDNA Murrows Review Form and must reference a previously awarded piece of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RTDNA staff will review submitted concerns and may escalate them to a review committee which evaluates issues under the Code of Ethics, best practices of journalism, and available process information. The review committee consists of individuals with RTDNA leadership experience and knowledge of Murrow Awards standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical awards delivery and recipient responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: RTDNA will mail regional plaques to the address listed on the entry form. You are responsible for reaching out to RTDNA to update your shipping information and are responsible for costs associated with misplaced or lost shipments due to incorrect information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should verify and, if needed, proactively update shipping addresses. Options exist to Order Replacement & Personalized Awards if needed.
